problem_text:
A municipality aims to formulate a coastal erosion mitigation strategy to diminish sediment loss from several vulnerable shoreline segments. Initially, no protective measures are in place.

The characteristics of each segment are as follows:
* For Segment A, erosion coefficient is 0.843, shoreline length is 63.123.
* For Segment B, erosion coefficient is 2.039, shoreline length is 153.325.
* For Segment C, erosion coefficient is 1.967, shoreline length is 229.34.
* For Segment D, erosion coefficient is 1.106, shoreline length is 75.136.
* For Segment E, erosion coefficient is 2.175, shoreline length is 242.692.
* For Segment F, erosion coefficient is 1.828, shoreline length is 51.295.
* For Segment G, erosion coefficient is 2.095, shoreline length is 187.588.

To counteract sediment loss, several stabilization techniques are available, each offering a specific retention efficacy:
* By deploying Technique 1, sediment loss will be curtailed by 16%
* By deploying Technique 2, sediment loss will be curtailed by 57%
* By deploying Technique 3, sediment loss will be curtailed by 15%
* By deploying Technique 4, sediment loss will be curtailed by 20%
* By deploying Technique 5, sediment loss will be curtailed by 52%
* By deploying Technique 6, sediment loss will be curtailed by 74%
* By deploying Technique 7, sediment loss will be curtailed by 13%

Implementing a technique on a segment entails an additional expenditure per unit length of shoreline. The cost matrix for all segment–technique pairings is provided below:

| Segment \ Technique | Technique1 | Technique2 | Technique3 | Technique4 | Technique5 | Technique6 | Technique7 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Segment A | 71.022 | 132.721 | 182.508 | 26.998 | 119.085 | 111.679 | 147.392 |
| Segment B | 187.967 | 183.514 | 43.262 | 177.627 | 43.4 | 184.731 | 199.463 |
| Segment C | 85.429 | 104.123 | 187.956 | 192.805 | 185.948 | 176.581 | 11.761 |
| Segment D | 117.913 | 30.387 | 196.769 | 64.067 | 197.929 | 113.227 | 103.843 |
| Segment E | 188.326 | 171.701 | 98.924 | 46.634 | 31.403 | 40.874 | 97.194 |
| Segment F | 58.88 | 45.378 | 149.957 | 160.246 | 117.878 | 153.884 | 43.344 |
| Segment G | 172.668 | 180.438 | 167.128 | 107.903 | 26.48 | 137.159 | 45.108 |

The planning authority must decide which techniques to apply to each segment (segments may employ multiple techniques concurrently), and a segment may also be left partially unprotected if required. The objective is to guarantee that the total sediment loss is reduced by at least a proportion P = 0.27 of the baseline loss, while minimizing the total implementation cost.
